items.title: Shelly Berg interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 15, 2000
items.q: He just threw out the first classical name he could think of, which was Debussy. But the sound he had in mind was Mozart.

ctx.x: It’s a true story. He gets on the scoring stage and he’s got LaMer nailed. And it’s gorgeous and the textures, and the cellos with five different parts. And he finishes and the orchestra is all tapping their bows, and the director walks up to him and says, “You know, I hate it. I just hate it.” So at that point the director said, “I want my mother” I think that’s the quote, that’s what he said, I want my mom. But he got with the director and what the composer found out was that the director really wanted Mozart.…
It’s all the same thing, isn’t it?
